summary: AE + SE from Redwood walked CedarPoint through dedicated GPU capacity model. Customer is evaluating dedicated vs hosted for productionizing a multi-model retrieval + generation service. Main drivers: data isolation, predictable throughput for peak trading hours, and tight p95 latency SLOs. Security team focused on KMS, audit logs, and VPC connectivity. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot benchmark on dedicated pool with defined burst window and autoscaling params. Next: pricing proposal, SOC2 docs, benchmark plan, follow-up security call.
topics: security and compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:30 UTC
Duration: 46m
Attendees: Olivia Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Anand Patel (Head of AI), Leah Ortiz (Infra Lead), Tom Reynolds (CISO)

[00:00] Olivia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Olivia from Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:08] Anand: Hey, Anand here, Head of AI at CedarPoint. We're evaluating options for moving our inference workloads off-prem.
[00:12] Leah: Leah, infra lead, I manage cluster and network stuff.
[00:15] Tom: Tom, CISO, I'll jump in on security requirements.
[00:18] Marcus: Marcus from Redwood SE, I'll do the technical deep dive when needed.
[00:23] Olivia: Cool, purpose of this call is to understand your needs for dedicated GPUs, isolation, burst, and scaling expectations.
[00:30] Anand: Right now we're running a mixed workload: retrieval-augmented generation for customer support and a smaller trading signals generation path. Peak QPS hits during market open - roughly 400 concurrent sessions, avg 2k tokens per session - so throughput matters.
[00:48] Leah: We need guaranteed isolation for compliance reasons; can't have noisy neighbors. VPC peering and customer-managed KMS are must-haves.
[00:58] Tom: Also full audit logs, long-term retention for certain events, and SSO/SAML integration, RBAC. We're SOC2 Type II in flight.
[01:11] Marcus: Got it. For dedicated we provide reserved GPU pools that are single-tenant per customer, with VPC connectivity and KMS/HSM options. We can surface audit logs and integrate with SSO.
[01:24] Anand: What's the typical sizing? 400 concurrent sessions, say peak 2.5k tokens/sec aggregate?
[01:31] Marcus: Rough rule: depends on model and quantization. For Llama 2-like model at 8-bit quant we can get higher packing, but if you need higher perf or lower latency we recommend 8x A100 or equivalent per 1000 concurrent short-chat style requests, but that's a rough.
[01:50] Leah: The trading workload wants p95 < 250ms for a single-turn generation, that's non-negotiable. Can you meet that on dedicated?
[01:59] Marcus: For shorter sequences and optimized kernels yes; with static batching and KV cache warm we can hit sub-200ms for some model configs. For long context you see latency growth. Also caching/prefix-KV helps a lot for repeated user prompts.
[02:15] Olivia: One thing customers do is reserve baseline GPUs sized for steady-state and configure a burst pool for market open. We can auto-route to burst pool when CPU/GPU utilization crosses threshold.
[02:26] Anand: How fast does burst scale up? We can't afford long cold starts during market open.
[02:31] Marcus: We have two mechanisms: warm standby (hot spares) which keeps instances ready - fast, little extra cost - or quick spin-up which is cheaper but ~2-5 minutes depending on infra. For your use-case we recommend warm standby for the critical window.
[02:44] Leah: What's the cost delta for warm standby?
[02:47] Marcus: Typically 15-30% premium on reserved baseline, depends on commit and instance types. We'll put numbers in the proposal.
[02:55] Tom: On encryption, our security policy requires customer-managed KMS and no plaintext logs leaving VPC. How do logs/audit work?
[03:04] Marcus: Audit events can be streamed to your logging endpoint, we support syslog and cloud logging endpoints. You can configure retention. We also support envelope encryption with your KMS.
[03:15] Anand: Any limitations around custom models? We want to bring our fine-tuned models and some open-source LLMs.
[03:22] Marcus: Dedicated supports custom model deployment; bring-your-own-model is supported. We handle model pinning, rollouts, and fallback to thinner quantized variants if capacity constrained.
[03:33] Leah: Networking - we need VPC peering with IP allowlist, and ideally no public egress for inference nodes. Can that be done?
[03:40] Marcus: Yes, Dedicated can be provisioned inside your VPC or via private peering with no public egress; that's a standard enterprise option.
[03:48] Olivia: Quick note, some transcription tools call KV cache 'K-V cash' in docs, so you might see typos in guides.
[03:55] Anand: (laughs) noted, we had that in our last eval too.
[04:00] Leah: What about autoscaling policies? We need predictable throughput but we also want to limit spend.
[04:06] Marcus: Autoscaling can be policy-driven: schedule-based scaling for known market windows, utilization-based with min/max pool sizes, and burst caps. You can set hard limits to prevent runaway costs.
[04:18] Anand: For the pilot, we want to emulate market open for 30 minutes with realistic traffic and measure p50/p95 and token cost.
[04:26] Olivia: That works. We'll propose a two-week pilot with a 3-day focused benchmark including that 30-minute window. Marcus will provide scripts.
[04:34] Tom: Liability - do you support dedicated control planes on-prem or VPC-hosted control plane? We have some customers that require private control plane.
[04:42] Marcus: For Private deployments yes; for Dedicated we offer VPC-hosted control plane with private endpoints. On-prem private deployments are available as an enterprise package.
[04:51] Anand: Does Redwood do model quantization for us or do we handle that?
[04:54] Marcus: We offer quantization recommendations and can run quantization as part of onboarding; we also provide compat builds for 4-bit/8-bit where applicable.
[05:03] Leah: Any common gotchas?
[05:05] Marcus: Warm cache warming is key. If you rely on cold starts, p95s spike. Also pay attention to sequence length distribution; billing and capacity both affected.
[05:15] Olivia: Ok let's capture next steps. We'll send a pricing + capacity proposal, Marcus will share benchmark runbook and scripts, and Tom we'll loop security to review SOC2 and KMS docs.
[05:25] Tom: We'll review. One more ask: can you share prior benchmarks for similar finance customers? Even anonymized numbers help.
[05:33] Marcus: Yes, we have redacted benchmark decks and a reference spreadsheet; will include links in the follow-up.
[05:41] Anand: Timeline-wise, if pilot looks good we expect procurement sign-off in 4-6 weeks.
[05:47] Olivia: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday with the docs.
[05:51] Leah: Thanks.
[05:53] Tom: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript. Notes: occasional transcription errors observed (model names mis-typed, KV cache sometimes 'K-V cash'), speaker overlaps minimal.
